Empires & Puzzles Miss Ethel Review: The Springvale Sniper Guide

Don't let the udders fool you; Miss Ethel hits like a freight train. We break down why this Springvale warrior's 600% hit and unique chain mechanic make her a situational nuke, even if she slows herself down in the process.
Miss Ethel: The Bovine Bazooka with a Chain Reaction
Miss Ethel: The Bovine Bazooka Who Moos For A Fight

Miss Ethel arrived in the Springvale 2024 event, bringing a refreshing (and slightly absurd) design to the roster. She is a 5-Star Legendary Ice hero from the Springvale family, and yes, she is an anthropomorphic cow with a giant mace. While the game takes itself seriously with eldritch horrors and grimdark goblins, Ethel is here to remind us that sometimes you just need to dress a cow in blue armor and have her smash things. She is a straightforward damage dealer who rewards you for hitting healthy enemies.

The art is undeniably memorable. We've gone from cute bunnies (Killhare) and majestic birds (Chick Jr... okay, maybe not majestic) to a full-on Minotaur-esque warrior. But unlike the fearsome Minotaur of Greek myth, Ethel has a certain "pastoral yet violent" charm. She wields a massive mace that looks like it could flatten a castle gate, yet she maintains a braided hairstyle that suggests she might have a shift at the dairy farm later. It's ridiculous, and we love it.

Miss Ethel is a hero who knows what she is: a cow with a mace who hits very, very hard. While she lacks the sophisticated passives and utility of the modern era, raw damage never truly goes out of style—it just finds a lower tier to dominate in. If you need a blue sniper who can occasionally wipe a team, she's your girl. Just don't ask her to hurry up; she moves at her own grazing pace.
A fun, hard-hitting relic of 2024. Level her for depth, but don't expect her to lead your defense team to the Top 100.
